backlog.spec: The current code feeds all ~210 RDKit descriptors into an RBF kernel after z-scoring, which lets dozens of near-duplicate counts dominate the distance metric. Replace it with a curated block of roughly 15-25 descriptors known to drive hepatic metabolism: MolLogP, MolMR, TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, FractionCSP3, NumAromaticRings, NumAliphaticRings, NumSaturatedRings, RingCount, HeavyAtomCount, NHOHCount, NOCount, BertzCT, BalabanJ, qed, plus counts of halogen, nitrogen and sulfur atoms and the number of aromatic nitrogen atoms. Z-score and clip as before, set gamma = 1/n_features, and keep the 0.5/0.5 mix with the Tanimoto kernel and the SVR unchanged. Rationale: an RBF kernel is a distance in the standardised descriptor space, so redundant and noisy descriptors directly degrade it; a compact mechanistically chosen block should give a sharper, better-conditioned similarity.
backlog.title: Curated physicochemical descriptor block replacing the full descList

backlog.spec: After the existing descriptor clip-and-standardize step, fit sklearn PCA(n_components=20, whiten=True, random_state=seed) on the training descriptor matrix D only, then transform both D and Dt. Clip the whitened components to [-5, 5]. Compute the RBF kernel on this 20-dimensional embedding with gamma = 1/20 instead of 1/n_descriptors. The Morgan Tanimoto kernel, the 0.5/0.5 mix, the SVR (C=5.0, epsilon=0.05) and the rank-normalized target are unchanged. This tests whether decorrelating the many redundant RDKit descriptors helps the RBF part of the kernel.
backlog.title: PCA-whitened descriptor embedding before the RBF kernel

backlog.spec: Fit 8 SVRs, each on a random 80% subset of training rows (rng from seed, indices sliced from K_train and K_test columns), and average the predictions. Keep the kernels and SVR parameters the same.
backlog.title: Bagged SVR on 80% subsamples

backlog.spec: After computing the SVR predictions, also fit lgb.LGBMRegressor on the standardized descriptors D plus the fingerprints (n_estimators=400, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=15, colsample_bytree=0.3, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, random_state=seed, verbose=-1). Fit it on the rank-transformed y. Return 0.6*rank(SVR) + 0.4*rank(LGBM), where rank uses rankdata on the test predictions.
backlog.title: Add LightGBM on descriptors, rank-averaged with SVR

backlog.spec: In train.py, keep the kernel mix unchanged and change the SVR hyperparameters to C=2.0 and epsilon=0.1 (target is rank-normalized and standardized, so these are sensible). Only change those two numbers in the SVR constructor.
backlog.title: SVR C and epsilon retune

backlog.spec: The Morgan bits currently reach the model only through the Tanimoto kernel, which is a similarity on sparse exact-substructure overlap and is weak when a test scaffold shares no bits with training. Give the smooth part of the model access to the same information in dense form: fit sklearn.decomposition.TruncatedSVD(n_components=64, random_state=seed) on the training Morgan bit matrix, transform both train and test, standardize those 64 components the same way as the descriptors, concatenate them with the standardized clipped RDKit descriptor block, and build the RBF kernel on the concatenation with gamma = 1.0 / (total number of columns). Keep the Morgan-Tanimoto kernel and the 0.5/0.5 mix, the rank-normalized target and the SVR settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Add a truncated-SVD compression of the Morgan bits to the descriptor kernel

backlog.spec: Change the kernel combination to 0.4*Tanimoto + 0.6*descriptor RBF in both K_train and K_test, since the descriptor kernel provided the largest gain.
backlog.title: Kernel mix weight 0.4/0.6

backlog.spec: In featurize(), replace the bit-vector output of GetMorganGenerator with occurrence counts: use gen.GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy(mol), and set RADIUS = 3 with N_BITS = 2048. The Tanimoto function already accepts non-negative real vectors, so the kernel code needs no change. Count fingerprints keep how often each substructure occurs, which often helps when the property scales with molecular size and substructure multiplicity.
backlog.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprints at radius 3

backlog.spec: In featurize(), build a second fingerprint block: 167 MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys, converted to a numpy array) and hashed atom-pair count fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator with fpSize=1024, GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy). Concatenate them with the Morgan bits and use the same Tanimoto kernel on the concatenated vector. Leave the descriptor RBF kernel and the 0.5 mixing weight unchanged. This gives the kernel a wider view of structure than Morgan alone.
backlog.title: Add MACCS keys and atom-pair counts to the kernel input

backlog.spec: Replace the single model with a proper stack. Base models: (1) kernel SVR on the current combined kernel, (2) LightGBM on Morgan fingerprint + descriptors, (3) RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=500, max_features=0.3, min_samples_leaf=2, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed) on the same matrix. Generate out-of-fold predictions for all three using an inner 5-fold KFold(shuffle=True, random_state=seed) on the training set, convert each column of OOF predictions to within-fold ranks, and fit a non-negative least squares or Ridge(alpha=1.0, positive=True) meta-model on the rank-transformed y. Refit each base model on the full training set, rank-transform their test predictions, and apply the learned meta weights. Rationale: hand-set blend weights are guesses; learned non-negative weights let the data decide how much each family is worth, and the ranks keep the meta-problem well scaled.
backlog.title: Out-of-fold stacking of three base models

backlog.spec: Keep the SVR-on-precomputed-kernel structure but widen the fingerprint part of the kernel. Instead of one Morgan radius-2 2048-bit fingerprint, compute three binary fingerprints per molecule with RDKit: Morgan radius 2 (2048 bits), Morgan radius 3 with features/pharmacophore-style invariants (GetMorganGenerator(radius=3, fpSize=2048, atomInvariantsGenerator=rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen())), and the RDKit path fingerprint (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetRDKitFPGenerator(fpSize=2048, maxPath=6)). Compute a Tanimoto similarity matrix for each and average the three into one structural kernel, then combine with the existing RBF-on-descriptors kernel as 0.5*K_struct + 0.5*K_rbf (same as now, just with the richer K_struct). Everything else, including the rank target transform and SVR(C=5, epsilon=0.05), stays identical. Rationale: single-radius ECFP is a narrow view of structure and path-based plus pharmacophore-typed fingerprints capture metabolic soft spots differently; averaging kernels is a cheap, well-conditioned way to combine them.
backlog.title: Multi-fingerprint Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Train a LightGBM regressor on the rank-transformed target (y - 0.5) / len(y) using objective='huber' with alpha=0.2 (LightGBM huber delta), along with min_child_samples=20, reg_lambda=5.0, colsample_bytree=0.3, and n_estimators=500 with learning_rate=0.03. The Huber loss reduces the influence of extreme clearance values, which the rank target only partly removes. Use the descriptors plus Morgan bits as features, and return the raw predictions. This is a standalone model that replaces the SVR.
backlog.title: Huber loss in LightGBM on the rank target

backlog.spec: Change featurize to use GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy with radius 2 and 2048 bits, which gives count vectors. Replace tanimoto with the MinMax kernel: sum(min(a,b)) / sum(max(a,b)). Compute it with a loop over test rows, or with the identity min(a,b) = (a+b-|a-b|)/2 in chunks. Use it in K_train and K_test in place of the binary Tanimoto.
backlog.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprints with MinMax kernel

backlog.spec: Keep the combined kernel K = 0.5*(tanimoto + rbf) on the Morgan bits and standardized RDKit descriptors. For each test molecule, take its 300 most similar training molecules by the combined kernel value (the kernel diagonal is 1 for the RBF part, so use the mean of the two kernel values as similarity). Fit a fresh SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5.0, epsilon=0.05) on only those 300 training molecules using the rank-normalized target standardized as before, then predict that single test molecule with it. Loop over test molecules. Fits are small (300 samples), so the 10-minute limit is not at risk. The global SVR is not used.
backlog.title: Local SVR specialist per test molecule

backlog.spec: Keep the current model but stop hard-coding the 0.5/0.5 kernel mix and C=5.0. Inside fit_predict, run a small inner 5-fold KFold (shuffle=True, random_state=seed) over the training molecules only, and grid-search the structural/descriptor mixing weight w in {0.25, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.75} and C in {1, 3, 10, 30}, scoring each candidate by mean Spearman correlation on the inner held-out folds. Compute the full train-train kernel matrices once outside the loop and index submatrices with np.ix_ so the search costs almost nothing. Refit on all training data with the best (w, C) and predict. Keep epsilon=0.05 and the rank target fixed to limit the search to 20 cells. Rationale: the current constants were never validated; the relative value of descriptor versus structural similarity is dataset-specific, and the inner search adapts it per fold at negligible runtime cost.
backlog.title: Tune kernel mixing weight and SVR C by inner CV

backlog.spec: Replace SVR with sklearn KernelRidge(kernel='precomputed', alpha=0.5) fit on the standardized rank targets. Alpha is the ridge strength. Return its predictions for K_test.
backlog.title: Kernel ridge / GP instead of SVR

backlog.spec: Add a second binary fingerprint from RDKit's Avalon toolkit: from rdkit.Avalon import pyAvalonTools, call pyAvalonTools.GetAvalonFP(mol, nBits=1024) for each molecule in train and test, and convert to a float numpy array. Define the Tanimoto kernel on these bits with the existing tanimoto() helper. Then set K = (1/3)*(tanimoto_morgan + tanimoto_avalon + rbf_descriptors), with the same gamma = 1/n_descriptors and the same SVR settings and rank target. Only the three-way average of kernels changes. If the Avalon import fails in the harness, fall back to the current two-kernel mix.
backlog.title: Avalon fingerprint Tanimoto kernel in the mix

backlog.spec: Before standardizing, apply a signed log1p transform, sign(x)*log1p(|x|), to the descriptor matrix D and Dt to tame heavy tails. Then drop descriptors whose absolute Spearman correlation with the rank target is below 0.05, computed on the training data only. Then proceed with the RBF kernel.
backlog.title: Log-transformed descriptors and feature selection

backlog.spec: After fitting the SVR, compute train-set out-of-sample-free residuals r = standardized y minus SVR train predictions is biased, so instead skip residuals and blend: final = 0.8*SVR prediction + 0.2*similarity-weighted mean of the training rank targets over the top 5 nearest training molecules by K_test (the mixed kernel), weights K_test values. Normalize both parts to ranks (rankdata/len) before blending.
backlog.title: Residual kNN correction

backlog.spec: The 0.5/0.5 split between the Morgan-Tanimoto kernel and the descriptor RBF kernel was never tuned, and picking a single weight by inner CV is noisy on fewer than 800 molecules. Instead, hedge: build K = w * Tanimoto + (1-w) * RBF for w in {0.35, 0.5, 0.65}, fit the same SVR (C=5, epsilon=0.05) on each of the three kernels, convert each set of test predictions to ranks with scipy.stats.rankdata, and return the mean of the three rank vectors divided by the number of test molecules. This costs three SVR solves (a few seconds) and should be at least as good as the best single weight while being far less sensitive to which weight that is.
backlog.title: Rank-average over three kernel mixing weights

backlog.spec: Keep the existing SVR prediction on the combined kernel. Also train a LightGBM regressor on the standardized descriptors plus Morgan bits (n_estimators=600, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=15, colsample_bytree=0.3, subsample=0.8 with subsample_freq=1, random_state=seed). Convert both prediction vectors to ranks within the test set with rankdata, then return the average of the two rank vectors scaled to [0, 1]. Rank averaging avoids having to calibrate the two model scales against each other.
backlog.title: Rank-averaged ensemble of the SVR kernel model and LightGBM

backlog.spec: Replace the binary Morgan fingerprint and its Tanimoto kernel with a count-based (hashed) Morgan fingerprint of radius 2 and 2048 bins (gen.GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy) and use the MinMax kernel, i.e. K(a,b) = sum_i min(a_i,b_i) / sum_i max(a_i,b_i), which is the natural generalisation of Tanimoto to counts. Implement it efficiently without a Python double loop: because counts are small, you can compute sum(min) via a loop over the handful of distinct count values, or just accept an O(n_train*n_test*2048) numpy broadcast in chunks of ~200 rows (970 molecules, this is fast enough). Keep everything else the same: descriptor RBF kernel, 0.5/0.5 mixing, rank target, SVR. Rationale: for clearance, the number of occurrences of a labile substructure (e.g. several benzylic positions) matters, and binary folding throws that away; MinMax preserves multiplicity while keeping the kernel positive semi-definite.
backlog.title: Count-based Morgan with MinMax kernel

backlog.spec: Add a third, very simple predictor and blend it in by rank. Using the Morgan Tanimoto similarity between test and train molecules, predict each test molecule as the similarity-weighted mean of the rank-transformed y of its k=15 nearest training neighbours, with weights sim**3 to sharpen the kernel and a floor so that a molecule with no close neighbour falls back to the training mean. Blend this kNN prediction with the existing SVR prediction as 0.75*rank(SVR) + 0.25*rank(kNN). Also return, implicitly, more robustness on the scaffold-split folds where the SVR extrapolates. Rationale: on scaffold-held-out folds the local similarity signal is weak but unbiased, while the global SVR can drift; a small weight on an explicit nearest-neighbour term is a cheap stabiliser and often adds a point of Spearman.
backlog.title: Add a scaffold-aware kNN similarity prior

backlog.spec: Fit SVR models at C in [1, 3, 10] on the same precomputed kernels. Average their predictions after rank-normalizing each one. This is a cheap ensemble that reduces sensitivity to C.
backlog.title: Inner-seed bagged SVR ensemble with different C

backlog.spec: The script currently maps y to rank-uniform values in [0,1] before fitting. Replace that with a monotone log transform of the raw measured value: y_t = log10(np.clip(y, small_positive, None)) where the clip floor is the 1st percentile of the positive training values, then standardise. Since Spearman only cares about ordering, any monotone transform is admissible, but the choice changes how the squared-error-based learner distributes its effort: rank-uniform spreads mass evenly, whereas log-clearance preserves the real gaps between fast and slow turnover compounds and can let the model focus on the chemically meaningful extremes. Keep the model, kernel and all hyperparameters identical so the comparison is clean, and report which transform wins.
backlog.title: Target transform study: log-clearance vs rank-uniform

backlog.spec: Keep K_train and K_test exactly as they are (0.5 * Tanimoto on Morgan bits + 0.5 * RBF on standardized descriptors). Swap the SVR for sklearn.kernel_ridge.KernelRidge(kernel='precomputed', alpha=1.0) and fit it on the standardized rank target (y - mu) / sd. Kernel ridge uses every training point with a squared loss, which can rank more smoothly than epsilon-insensitive SVR on small datasets. Choose alpha from {0.1, 0.3, 1, 3} by inner 5-fold CV on the training fold only, maximizing Spearman.
backlog.title: Replace SVR with kernel ridge regression on the same combined kernel

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, apply an elementwise power 1.5 to the Tanimoto kernel matrices (both train and test) before averaging with the RBF descriptor kernel: tanimoto(X,X)**1.5 and tanimoto(Xt,X)**1.5. Leave the rest unchanged.
backlog.title: Sharpened Tanimoto kernel power

backlog.spec: The target is currently mapped to uniform (rank-0.5)/n values. Replace that with a van der Waerden normal-score transform: y = scipy.stats.norm.ppf((rankdata(y) - 0.5) / n), then standardize as now before fitting the SVR. This keeps the rank order (so the Spearman score is unaffected by the monotone change itself) but spreads the extreme molecules further apart and compresses the dense middle, which changes which samples become support vectors under the epsilon-insensitive loss. Only the two lines that build the transformed target need to change; the kernel mix, C=5 and epsilon=0.05 stay as they are.
backlog.title: Normal-score target transform instead of uniform ranks

backlog.spec: The descriptor side currently enters only through a local RBF kernel, which decays quickly and gives almost no signal for test molecules far from the training set, a common situation under scaffold splits. Add a third kernel: L2-normalize the standardized, clipped descriptor rows and take their dot product (a cosine/linear kernel, values in [-1,1], optionally shifted to [0,1] by (1+cos)/2). Mix the three kernels with equal weights 1/3 Morgan-Tanimoto, 1/3 descriptor RBF, 1/3 descriptor cosine, for both the train-train and test-train matrices. The cosine term is global and smooth and should extrapolate better to unseen scaffolds. Keep the rank-normalized target and the SVR (C=5, epsilon=0.05).
backlog.title: Add a cosine kernel on descriptors as a third kernel

backlog.spec: Change the kernel mix from 0.5/0.5 to a weighted one. Use 0.35 for Tanimoto and 0.65 for the RBF on descriptors. Descriptors usually matter more for clearance, which depends on lipophilicity and similar properties. Make the weight a constant W_FP.
backlog.title: Weighted kernel mix

memo: Helped: changing model family (LightGBM 0.5726, Tanimoto-kernel SVR 0.5491, from 0.6103 start), rank-normalizing the target (0.5310/0.5307, replicated), and above all averaging the Tanimoto kernel with an RDKit 2D descriptor RBF kernel (0.4830, incumbent). Did not help: FCFP (0.5877), MACCS (0.5421), stacking (0.5558), MLP ensemble (0.5500), descriptor-only ridge (0.5328), 60-descriptor subset (0.4973), autocorrelation descriptors (0.5057), RankSVM (0.5957), Laplacian solve (0.5716). Within noise (sd about 0.0070): scaffold weighting 0.4803, KernelRidge 0.4822, descriptor weighting 0.4824, extra kernels (0.4854-0.4860). Gobbi kernel (0.4680/0.4791) and ridge prior (0.4711/0.4728) were borderline gains that did not hold up on replication. Kernels look plateaued near 0.48. Next: tune SVR C, epsilon and descriptor gamma; try a GP; try quantile-transformed descriptors; maybe combine Gobbi with the ridge prior. Read train.py first, since many edits aborted by assuming a random forest or LightGBM. Replicate gains under 0.01.
